title: WPSS/1689/2021 of SHAKUNTALA ARYA Vs DISTRICT MAGISTRATE UDAHM SINGH SINGH

COURT'S OR JUDGES'S ORDERS
WPSS No.1689 of 2021
Hon 'b le Sh ar ad Ku m ar Sh ar m a, J.
Mr. Naman Kamboj, Advocate, for the
petitioner.
 Mr. Sushil Vashistha, Brief Holder, for
the State of Uttarakhand.

The petitioner to the present petition has
prayed for issuing a writ of mandamus
commanding the respondents to grant
compassionate appointment to the petitioner,
who is the widowed daughter-in-law of the
family of Late Smt. Nirmala.
The brief facts of the case are that the
petitioner's marriage was solemnized with one
Mr. Yogesh Kumar, who had met with the sad
demise on 04.11.2004. The petitioner contends
that she is the daughter-in-law of the deceased
employee Smt. Nirmala, and her Late husband
i.e. Mr. Yogesh Kumar Arya. Smt. Nirmala was
given an appointment in the office of the
respondents. Ultimately the mother-in-law of
the petitioner i.e. Smt. Nirmala too, had met
with the sad demise on 02.08.2020.
 As a consequence thereto, the petitioner,
who is daughter-in-law of Late Smt. Nirmala,
and the wife of Late Mr. Yogesh Kumar Arya,
is the only surviving heirs in the family of her
in-laws, on whom the entire responsibility of

the family has befallen. Coupled with the fact
that, she has to cater day-to-day needs of the
family, and has also to shoulder the
responsibility to maintain two grown up
children of 17 years and 15 years of age
respectively.
 However, her claim for the consideration
for grant of a compassionate appointment on
the death of the late Smt. Nirmala, the mother-in-law of the petitioner, was denied on the
ground that she would not be falling within a
definition of family, as provided under the
Dying in Harness Rules of 1974, and she was
rendered to be non suited for consideration for
being granted an appointment on
compassionate ground, as the daughter-in-law
does not find place in the definition of the
family as provided under Section 2 (c) of the
Rules of 1974.
Petitioner contends, that this
discrimination made at the hands of the
respondents to deny the candidature of the
petitioner merely because of the fact that she is
daughter-in-law of Late Smt. Nirmala, and she
is outside the ambit of the family, as defined
under the Rules of 1974.
In order to meet out the said objection,
the learned counsel for the petitioner had made
a reference to a Full Bench Judgement of the
Allahabad High Court, as rendered in Special

Appeal No. 1026 of 2003, "U.P. Power
Corporation, Urban Electricity Transmission
Division - H, Allahabad Vs. Urmila Devi",
wherein, the Full Bench Judgement of the
Allahabad High Court in its paragraph No.7,
has observed that it is absolutely unacceptable
fact and preposition of law that when a widow
daughter is brought within the ambit of the
family, why not the widow daughter-in-law
could be taken into consideration as to be part
of the family of in laws, and brought within the
definition of the family for the purposes of
considering her candidature to be appointed on
compassionate ground. The relevant
observations made in paragraph Nos. 7 of the
judgement is extracted hereunder:-
"We must, however, note one feature
of the definition of the word family' as
generally contained in most Rules. The
definition of family' includes wife or
husband; sons; unmarried and
widowed daughters; and if the
deceased was an unmarried
government servant, the brother,
unmarried sister and widowed mother
dependant on the deceased
government servant. It is, therefore,
clear that a widowed daughter in the
house of her parents is entitled for
consideration on compassionate
appointment. However, a widowed
daughter-in-law in the house where
she is married, is not entitled for
compassionate appointment as she is
not included in the definition of
'family'. It is not possible to
understand how a widowed daughter

in her father's house has a better right
to claim appointment on
compassionate basis than a widowed
daughter-in-law in her father-in-law's
house. The very nature of
compassionate appointment is the
financial need or necessity of the
family. The daughter-in-law on the
death of her husband does not cease to
be a part of the family. The concept
that such daughter-in-law must go
back and stay with her parents is
abhorrent to our civilized society.
Such daughter-in-law must, therefore,
have also right to be considered for
compassionate appointment as she is
part of the family where she is married
and if staying with her husband's
family. In this context, in our
opinion, arbitrariness, as presently
existing, can be avoided by including
the daughter-in-law in the definition of
'family'. Otherwise, the definition to
that extent, prima facie, would be
irrational and arbitrary. The State,
therefore, to consider this aspect and
take appropriate steps so that a
widowed daughter-in-law like a
widowed daughter, is also entitled for
consideration by way of
compassionate appointment, if other
criteria is satisfied."
In view of the aforesaid observations,
which has been made in the judgement of the
Full Bench of the Allahabad High Court,
wherein, daughter-in-law has been brought
within the definition of the family of the
deceased employee, this Court is of the view
that, there is no plausible reasons for this Court
not to agree with the ratio of the Full Bench

judgement as dealt with in paragraph No.7, of
the judgement dated 27.01.2011.
Hence, this writ petition too would stands
disposed of with a direction to the respondents
to consider the petitioner's candidature for
appointment on compassionate ground, based
on the principles and the observations which
had been made in paragraph No.7, of the
judgement of the Full Bench of the Allahabad
High Court, as referred above.
It is expected that the respondents would
consider, and take a decision on the petitioner's
claim for compassionate appointment, as
expeditiously as possible, but not later than two
months from the date of the production of a
certified copy of this judgement.
Subject to the aforesaid observations the
writ petition stands disposed of.

( Sh ar ad Ku m ar Sh ar m a, J.)
 27.12.2021
